---
title: "A single-cell workflow with every subset in one object"
description: >
  From raw droplets to T-cell subtypes in 4,000 PBMCs, keeping three sets
  of cell calls, high-quality cells, variable genes and T cells as subsets
  of one ExperimentSubset object.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 5)
```

A single-cell analysis makes many versions of the same data: all droplets,
the droplets that hold cells, the cells that pass quality control, the
genes that vary most, a cell type re-analysed on its own. Usually each
becomes a separate object, and each copy has to be kept in step with the
others.

This article runs a complete analysis of 4,000 peripheral blood
mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 10x Genomics and keeps every one of those
versions as a **subset** of one `ExperimentSubset` object. A subset stores
which rows and columns of its parent it uses, plus anything computed for
it. It sees its parent's assays without copying them.

The purpose of this article is to show how a whole analysis fits in one
object, not to give a complete or definitive annotation of PBMCs. The
quality-control thresholds and the cell-type labels are simple, common
choices; a careful annotation would need more work, such as checking
marker genes for each cluster.

The analysis takes about 15 minutes and downloads about 200 MB the first
time it runs.

We store results in two ways, and each step says which it uses:

- **Experiment style.** `getSubsetExperiment()` takes a subset out as an
  ordinary `SingleCellExperiment`; we run any tool on it, and
  `setSubsetExperiment()` stores the result back in the subset: its
  assays, colData, rowData, reducedDims and metadata replace the
  subset's own.
- **Direct style.** We compute a result ourselves and store it in the
  subset with `setSubsetAssay()`, `colData()`, `rowData()` or
  `reducedDim()` with `subsetName =`.

The names of the subsets, assays and reduced dimensions follow the
[MAMS](https://github.com/single-cell-mams/mams) conventions; the last
section shows how they map.

# The data

We use the PBMC 4k data set, processed with Cell Ranger 2.1.0, from the
DropletTestFiles package. It has two matrices: the *raw* matrix, with
every droplet barcode, most of them empty, and the *filtered* matrix,
with the droplets that Cell Ranger called as cells.

```{r download}
library(DropletTestFiles)

# download both matrices (cached after the first time)
rawFile <- getTestFile("tenx-2.1.0-pbmc4k/1.0.0/raw.tar.gz")
filteredFile <- getTestFile("tenx-2.1.0-pbmc4k/1.0.0/filtered.tar.gz")

# unpack them into a temporary folder
dataFolder <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbmc4k")
untar(rawFile, exdir = dataFolder)
untar(filteredFile, exdir = dataFolder)
```

```{r read}
library(DropletUtils)

# read each matrix, naming the columns by barcode
rawFolder <- file.path(dataFolder, "raw_gene_bc_matrices", "GRCh38")
filteredFolder <- file.path(dataFolder, "filtered_gene_bc_matrices", "GRCh38")
raw <- read10xCounts(rawFolder, col.names = TRUE)
filtered <- read10xCounts(filteredFolder, col.names = TRUE)
dim(raw)
dim(filtered)
```

The rows are named by Ensembl ID. Gene symbols are easier to read, so we
use them instead, keeping the Ensembl ID where a symbol is repeated.

```{r symbols}
library(scuttle)

# use gene symbols as row names
geneIds <- rowData(raw)$ID
geneSymbols <- rowData(raw)$Symbol
geneNames <- uniquifyFeatureNames(geneIds, geneSymbols)
rownames(raw) <- geneNames
```

# One object for all droplets

`ExperimentSubset()` wraps the raw `SingleCellExperiment`. Its main assay,
`counts`, holds every droplet. The cells Cell Ranger found become the
first subset, `filtered`, chosen by barcode.

```{r object}
library(ExperimentSubset)

# all droplets in the main object
es <- ExperimentSubset(raw)

# the droplets Cell Ranger called as cells
cellBarcodes <- colnames(filtered)
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "filtered", cols = cellBarcodes)
es
```

`assay(es, "filtered")` returns the counts of the filtered cells. They are
not copied: the subset stores the column positions and reads the main
object's counts when asked.

# Finding cells among the droplets

*On the main object.* `es` is itself a `SingleCellExperiment`, so tools
can run on it directly. singleCellTK's `runDropletQC()` runs two other
methods from DropletUtils on every droplet: `emptyDrops`, which tests each
droplet against the ambient RNA profile, and `barcodeRanks`, which finds
the knee in the curve of total counts. We leave out its third method,
per-droplet QC metrics, which is slow on 737,280 droplets; we compute QC
metrics for the cells below. emptyDrops uses random sampling, so we set a
seed first.

```{r droplet-qc}
library(singleCellTK)

# test every droplet; set a seed, since emptyDrops samples at random
set.seed(100)
es <- runDropletQC(es, algorithms = c("emptyDrops", "barcodeRanks"))
```

Each method gives its own set of cells: emptyDrops' calls at a false
discovery rate of 1%, and the droplets above barcodeRanks' knee.

```{r droplet-calls}
# droplets that emptyDrops calls as cells
dropletFdr <- colData(es)$dropletUtils_emptyDrops_fdr
emptyDropsCell <- !is.na(dropletFdr) & dropletFdr <= 0.01

# droplets above the knee of the barcode-rank curve
kneeCell <- colData(es)$dropletUtils_BarcodeRank_Knee == 1

# droplets that Cell Ranger called as cells
cellRangerCell <- colnames(es) %in% cellBarcodes
table(emptyDrops = emptyDropsCell, cellRanger = cellRangerCell)
```

We keep each set of calls as a subset next to Cell Ranger's `filtered`. A
subset stores only the positions of its droplets, so the object barely
grows.

```{r droplet-subsets}
# size of the object before
format(object.size(es), units = "MB")

# emptyDrops' and barcodeRanks' cells as two more subsets
emptyDropsPositions <- which(emptyDropsCell)
kneePositions <- which(kneeCell)
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "emptydrops", cols = emptyDropsPositions)
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "barcoderanks", cols = kneePositions)

# size of the object after
format(object.size(es), units = "MB")

# the number of genes and cells in each set of calls
subsetDim(es, subsetName = "filtered")
subsetDim(es, subsetName = "emptydrops")
subsetDim(es, subsetName = "barcoderanks")
```

The three mostly agree. We continue with Cell Ranger's calls, the
`filtered` subset; the others stay in the object for comparison.

# Quality control of the cells

*Experiment style.* `getSubsetExperiment()` returns the `filtered` subset
as an ordinary `SingleCellExperiment`, with the main object's colData
columns (the droplet QC above) included.

```{r get-filtered}
# the filtered cells as a SingleCellExperiment
filteredCells <- getSubsetExperiment(es, subsetName = "filtered")
filteredCells
```

singleCellTK's `runCellQC()` computes per-cell QC metrics, including the
percentage of counts from mitochondrial genes, and finds doublets with
scDblFinder. Our row names are gene symbols, so we say so. scDblFinder
samples at random; `runCellQC()` sets its own seed (`seed = 12345` by
default), so the results are the same on every run.

```{r cell-qc}
# QC metrics and doublet calls for each cell
filteredCells <- runCellQC(filteredCells,
                           algorithms = c("QCMetrics", "scDblFinder"),
                           mitoIDType = "symbol")
```

`setSubsetExperiment()` stores what `runCellQC()` added in the `filtered`
subset. The counts are unchanged, so they are not copied, and neither are
the main object's colData columns.

```{r set-filtered}
# store the QC results in the subset
es <- setSubsetExperiment(es, subsetName = "filtered", value = filteredCells)
colnames(colData(es, subsetName = "filtered"))
```

# Removing ambient RNA

*Direct style.* celda's `decontX()` estimates how much of each cell's
counts comes from ambient RNA, the free-floating RNA in every droplet, and
removes it. It estimates the ambient profile from the cells themselves.
Like `runCellQC()`, `decontX()` sets its own seed by default.

```{r decontx}
library(celda)

# counts of the cells
cellCounts <- assay(es, "filtered")

# estimate and remove the ambient RNA
decontamination <- decontX(cellCounts)
```

The decontaminated counts become an assay of the `filtered` subset, and
the estimated contamination becomes a colData column.

```{r store-decontx}
# store the decontaminated counts in the subset
decontaminatedCounts <- decontamination$decontXcounts
es <- setSubsetAssay(es, subsetName = "filtered",
                     inputMatrix = decontaminatedCounts,
                     subsetAssayName = "decontaminated")

# store each cell's contamination with its other QC columns
colData(es, subsetName = "filtered")$contamination <-
  decontamination$contamination
```

# Keeping high-quality cells

We keep cells that have at least 300 detected genes, at most 10% of
counts from mitochondrial genes, at most 30% contamination, and that
scDblFinder calls singlets.

```{r filter}
# the QC columns of the filtered cells
filteredData <- colData(es, subsetName = "filtered")

# each QC rule
enoughGenes <- filteredData$detected >= 300
lowMito <- filteredData$mito_percent <= 10
lowContamination <- filteredData$contamination <= 0.3
singlet <- filteredData$scDblFinder_doublet_call == "Singlet"

# cells that pass all of them
keepCells <- enoughGenes & lowMito & lowContamination & singlet
table(keepCells)
```

The new subset, `clean`, is made from the decontaminated counts: its
`parentAssay` is `"filtered/decontaminated"`, the assay `decontaminated`
stored in the subset `filtered`.

```{r clean}
# the high-quality cells, from the decontaminated counts
cellsToKeep <- which(keepCells)
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "clean", cols = cellsToKeep,
                   parentAssay = "filtered/decontaminated")
subsetDim(es, subsetName = "clean")
```

# Clustering

*Direct style.* We follow a standard workflow with the scrapper package,
storing each result in the `clean` subset or in its subset of variable
genes.

**Normalisation.** Counts are divided by each cell's size factor and
log-transformed. `delayed = FALSE` computes the values now, rather than
each time they are read.

```{r normalize}
library(scrapper)

# decontaminated counts of the clean cells
cleanCounts <- assay(es, "clean")

# size factors from each cell's total, then log-normalised values
cellTotals <- colSums(cleanCounts)
sizeFactors <- centerSizeFactors(cellTotals)
lognormalized <- normalizeCounts(cleanCounts, sizeFactors, delayed = FALSE)
es <- setSubsetAssay(es, subsetName = "clean",
                     inputMatrix = lognormalized,
                     subsetAssayName = "lognormalized")
```

**Variable genes.** We choose the 2,000 genes whose expression varies
most across the clean cells, and keep them as a subset of rows,
`clean.variable`, made from the log-normalised values.

```{r variable-genes}
# variance of each gene, and the 2,000 most variable
geneVariances <- modelGeneVariances(lognormalized)
geneResiduals <- geneVariances$statistics$residuals
variableGenes <- chooseHighlyVariableGenes(geneResiduals, top = 2000)

# the variable genes as a subset of rows
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "clean.variable", rows = variableGenes,
                   parentAssay = "clean/lognormalized")
variableLognormalized <- assay(es, "clean.variable")
dim(variableLognormalized)
```

**Scaling.** Each variable gene's log-normalised values are turned into
z-scores across the clean cells: mean 0 and standard deviation 1. Only
the variable genes are scaled: only they go into the PCA, and z-scores,
which are rarely zero, take far more memory than the sparse log-normalised
values. The z-scores are stored in the `clean.variable` subset.

```{r scale}
# z-scores of each variable gene; scale() works on columns, so we
# transpose to one column per gene and back
variableDense <- as.matrix(variableLognormalized)
genesByColumn <- t(variableDense)
scaledByColumn <- scale(genesByColumn)
scaled <- t(scaledByColumn)
es <- setSubsetAssay(es, subsetName = "clean.variable",
                     inputMatrix = scaled,
                     subsetAssayName = "scaled")
```

**PCA, clusters and UMAP.** We keep the first 25 principal components
(scrapper's default) of the z-scores. They describe the clean cells, so
we store them, the clusters and the UMAP in the `clean` subset.
`runPca()` returns them with one column per cell, the layout the other
scrapper functions take; reduced dimensions are stored with one row per
cell, so we transpose them for storing. scrapper's PCA, clustering and
UMAP use fixed seeds by default, so they give the same results on every
run.

```{r pca}
# principal components of the z-scores of the variable genes
pca <- runPca(scaled)
cellPcs <- t(pca$components)
reducedDim(es, "reduction.pca", subsetName = "clean") <- cellPcs
```

```{r cluster}
# a nearest-neighbour graph of the cells, and its clusters
neighbourGraph <- buildSnnGraph(pca$components)
clusters <- clusterGraph(neighbourGraph)

# a two-dimensional UMAP embedding
umap <- runUmap(pca$components)
reducedDim(es, "embedding.umap", subsetName = "clean") <- umap
```

# Annotating cell types

*Direct style.* SingleR labels each cell with the most similar cell type
in a reference, here the Monaco immune reference from celldex.

```{r singler}
library(SingleR)
library(celldex)

# the reference, and the predicted main cell type of each clean cell
monaco <- MonacoImmuneData()
cleanLognormalized <- assay(es, "clean/lognormalized")
predictions <- SingleR(test = cleanLognormalized, ref = monaco,
                       labels = monaco$label.main)
```

The clusters and labels go into the `clean` subset's colData, and a few
known marker genes are flagged in its rowData.

```{r store-labels}
# clusters and labels in the subset's colData
colData(es, subsetName = "clean")$cluster <- clusters$membership
colData(es, subsetName = "clean")$label <- predictions$labels
table(predictions$labels)

# marker genes flagged in the subset's rowData
markers <- c("CD3E", "CD4", "CD8A", "MS4A1", "CD14", "FCGR3A", "NKG7",
             "LYZ", "PPBP")
cleanGenes <- subsetRownames(es, subsetName = "clean")
rowData(es, subsetName = "clean")$marker <- cleanGenes %in% markers
```

We take the subset out again to plot it with scater.

```{r plot-clean, fig.alt = "UMAP of the clean cells, coloured by cell type"}
library(scater)

# the clean cells, coloured by cell type
cleanCells <- getSubsetExperiment(es, subsetName = "clean")
plotReducedDim(cleanCells, dimred = "embedding.umap", colour_by = "label")
```

# Re-analysing the T cells

*Experiment style.* T cells are the largest group. We make them a subset
of `clean`, then repeat the analysis on them alone.

```{r tcells}
# the clean cells labelled as T cells
tcellLabels <- c("CD4+ T cells", "CD8+ T cells", "T cells")
isTcell <- predictions$labels %in% tcellLabels
tcellPositions <- which(isTcell)
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "tcells", cols = tcellPositions,
                   parentAssay = "clean")
subsetDim(es, subsetName = "tcells")
```

The new subset already sees the assays of `clean`, and those `clean` sees
in turn, linked rather than copied:

```{r tcell-assays}
subsetAssayNames(es, subsetName = "tcells")
```

A cell's log-normalised values depend on its own counts and size factor,
so the T cells reuse `lognormalized` from `clean`, as subclustering
usually does. The variable genes and their z-scores depend on which cells
are included, so we compute them again on the T cells.

```{r get-tcells}
# the T cells as a SingleCellExperiment, with the linked assays
tcells <- getSubsetExperiment(es, subsetName = "tcells")
assayNames(tcells)
```

```{r tcell-variable}
# the 2,000 genes that vary most among T cells
tcellLognormalized <- assay(tcells, "lognormalized")
tcellVariances <- modelGeneVariances(tcellLognormalized)
tcellResiduals <- tcellVariances$statistics$residuals
tcellVariableGenes <- chooseHighlyVariableGenes(tcellResiduals, top = 2000)
```

```{r tcell-scale}
# z-scores of the T cells' variable genes, across the T cells only
tcellVariableLognormalized <- tcellLognormalized[tcellVariableGenes, ]
tcellDense <- as.matrix(tcellVariableLognormalized)
tcellGenesByColumn <- t(tcellDense)
tcellScaledByColumn <- scale(tcellGenesByColumn)
tcellScaled <- t(tcellScaledByColumn)
```

```{r tcell-cluster}
# principal components, stored with one row per cell
tcellPca <- runPca(tcellScaled)
tcellPcs <- t(tcellPca$components)
reducedDim(tcells, "reduction.pca") <- tcellPcs

# clusters of the T cells
tcellGraph <- buildSnnGraph(tcellPca$components)
tcellClusters <- clusterGraph(tcellGraph)
tcells$cluster <- tcellClusters$membership

# a UMAP embedding of the T cells
tcellUmap <- runUmap(tcellPca$components)
reducedDim(tcells, "embedding.umap") <- tcellUmap
```

```{r tcell-singler}
# the T-cell part of the reference, so every cell gets a T-cell subtype
isTcellReference <- monaco$label.main %in% tcellLabels
tcellReference <- monaco[, isTcellReference]

# finer T-cell subtypes
tcellPredictions <- SingleR(test = tcellLognormalized, ref = tcellReference,
                            labels = tcellReference$label.fine)
tcells$subtype <- tcellPredictions$labels
table(tcells$subtype)
```

`setSubsetExperiment()` stores the reduced dimensions and colData columns
we added in the `tcells` subset. The assays are unchanged, so they stay
linked and nothing is copied.

```{r set-tcells}
# store the T-cell results
es <- setSubsetExperiment(es, subsetName = "tcells", value = tcells)
```

As for the clean cells, the T cells' variable genes become a subset of
rows, `tcells.variable`, which stores their z-scores.

```{r tcells-variable}
# the T cells' variable genes, and their z-scores
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "tcells.variable",
                   rows = tcellVariableGenes,
                   parentAssay = "tcells/lognormalized")
es <- setSubsetAssay(es, subsetName = "tcells.variable",
                     inputMatrix = tcellScaled,
                     subsetAssayName = "scaled")
```

`clean.variable` and `tcells.variable` each store their own `scaled`: an
assay stored in one subset doesn't clash with one of the same name in
another. A subset can't store an assay under a name it already sees
linked from its parent, though; replacing, say, the T cells'
`lognormalized` with values computed on the T cells alone would need
`unlink = TRUE`, after which `tcells` and the subsets made from it use
their own version.

```{r plot-tcells, fig.alt = "UMAP of the T cells, coloured by T-cell subtype"}
# the T cells, coloured by subtype
tcellCells <- getSubsetExperiment(es, subsetName = "tcells")
plotReducedDim(tcellCells, dimred = "embedding.umap", colour_by = "subtype")
```

# The whole analysis in one object

`subsetSummary()` lists every subset, what it was made from, and what it
stores.

```{r summary}
subsetSummary(es)
```

All of this lives in one object. The subsets store row and column
positions, and only what was computed for them: `decontaminated` in
`filtered`, `lognormalized` in `clean`, `scaled` in the two variable-gene
subsets, and the colData, rowData and reduced dimensions added along the
way. A linked assay, such as the T cells' `lognormalized`, is only built
when it is read.

```{r size}
# the whole object
format(object.size(es), units = "MB")

# the counts of all 737,280 droplets, stored once
allCounts <- assay(es, "counts")
format(object.size(allCounts), units = "MB")
```

Kept as separate objects instead, the three sets of cell calls, the clean
cells and the T cells would each carry their own copy of the counts, and
the T cells another copy of the log-normalised values.

# How this maps to MAMS

[MAMS](https://github.com/single-cell-mams/mams) (Matrix and Analysis
Metadata Standards) describes the matrices and annotations a single-cell
analysis produces. The names used here follow its suggested values where
it has them (`filtered`, `clean`, `variable`, `counts`, `lognormalized`,
`scaled`, `reduction`, `embedding`); `emptydrops`, `barcoderanks` and
`tcells` are our own names for subsets.

| In this article | ExperimentSubset | MAMS |
|---|---|---|
| `filtered`, `emptydrops`, `barcoderanks`, `clean`, `tcells` | subsets of columns | `obs_subset` |
| `clean.variable`, `tcells.variable` | subsets of rows | `feature_subset` (`variable`) |
| `counts`, `decontaminated`, `lognormalized`, `scaled` | assays | `processing` |
| `reduction.pca`, `embedding.umap` | reducedDims | `processing` (`reduction`, `embedding`) |
| `parentAssay`, e.g. `"filtered/decontaminated"` | the assay or subset a subset was made from | `parent_id` |
| a subset made from its parent's rows or columns | `createSubset()` | `parent_relationship` (`subset`) |
